name: Approved run → project the change's tasks into immutable task.spec
description:
The projection station (R6, group 6 — now a publish-triggered COMPONENT). The dev-from-task spec requires: WHEN run.change.decision == "approve" is present for a run, THEN the change's tasks are projected as immutable task.spec facts (the dev loop converges on them, it does not redefine them). This rule is that trigger. It fires on the RUN entity after the human-approval gate releases (the approve decision present, the run resumed to executing) and fires a plain `publish` to component.projection-station.dispatch — the PROJECTION STATION component reads the change's authored task facts off the run, enforces the Karpathy task schema, clamps each iteration budget to [1,5], binds to the VALIDATED content (D15 #0: it freezes only when openspec.change.validated equals openspec.change.<slug>.revision), and stamps the immutable task.spec.<i>.* package — or fails toward the human on a schema gap, with ZERO model turns (the projection replaced its forced coordinator loop, R6). G2: this rule fires no lifecycle transition; the projection component writes evidence facts (via the shared projecttasks.Project core the old tool used — one writer, G5).

RUN BINDING: the rule fires on the RUN entity, so the rule engine's executePublish stamps the dispatch payload's entity_id = the run entity id (dev-from-task/01-anchor-run-for-dispatch stamps the agent.loop.run anchor first; this rule requires agent.loop.run ne "" so it fires only once that anchor is present, which is also why the run resolves). The projection station reads req.EntityID (the run) and stamps task.spec on it.

SLUG THREADING: project_tasks needs the change slug as a value (the run's change facts are slug-SCOPED, openspec.change.<slug>.*, so a rule cannot wildcard the slug out of the predicate key). create_change stamps a run-level slug pointer openspec.change.slug=<slug>; this rule threads it into the publish as the `slug` property ($entity.triple.openspec.change.slug), which the station reads.

ORDERING (before the dev re-wake): the dev-loop kickoff re-wake (dev-from-task/02) is gated behind projection COMPLETION (it requires task.spec.test-command ne ""), so this projection runs first and the coordinator re-wakes only once task.spec exists — which its prompt assumes ('read the projected task specs').

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps the fired-once marker run.projection.kickoff=$entity.instance on the run, and the run.projection.kickoff length_eq 0 guard makes the trigger flip false the moment it fires. This is the house restart-safety pattern: the publish is not deduped (core NATS) and the other trigger conditions (agent.loop.run/executing/approved) stay true, so WITHOUT this marker a graph replay with RULE_STATE lost would re-dispatch a DUPLICATE projection. The marker (a durable ENTITY_STATES triple) closes that independent of RULE_STATE. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish so a publish failure leaves the run stuck rather than duplicated; project_tasks's task.spec immutability is a second guard. KNOWN M0 GAP (honest, general to all R6 stations): because the marker is set before the effect and rules are edge-triggered, a PERSISTENT projection refusal (schema gap after the station's bounded retry) leaves the marker set + task.spec absent with nothing to re-trigger — the run does NOT auto-park at M0. The routed-without-result reconciliation is R8/group 8.

metadata.station: projection-station — freeze the approved change's tasks into immutable task.spec (R6 component)
metadata.trigger_rationale: spec: WHEN run.change.decision == "approve" present THEN tasks projected. Fires on the RUN entity at approval, requiring the agent.loop.run anchor (dev-from-task/01) so the run resolves and executePublish stamps the run as the dispatch entity_id.
metadata.mechanism: R6: a plain `publish` to component.projection-station.dispatch triggers the projection STATION component (zero model turns), replacing the forced project_tasks coordinator turn. The rule engine emits it on core NATS (the rule component declares no matching JetStream output port).
metadata.slug_threading: the projection station needs the slug as a value; the run's change facts are slug-scoped so a rule cannot wildcard it. create_change stamps openspec.change.slug=<slug> (run-level pointer, its owned namespace) and this rule threads $entity.triple.openspec.change.slug as the `slug` publish property.
metadata.ordering: runs BEFORE the dev re-wake (dev-from-task/02 is gated on task.spec.test-command ne ""), so the coordinator re-wakes only after task.spec exists.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the run.projection.kickoff marker + length_eq 0 guard (house pattern). The core-NATS publish is not deduped, so the marker keeps the dispatch fire-once even under RULE_STATE loss; projecttasks.Project's task.spec immutability is a second guard.
metadata.known_gap: general R6 station gap (honest): a PERSISTENT projection refusal (schema gap after the station's bounded retry) leaves run.projection.kickoff set + task.spec absent with nothing to re-trigger — the run does NOT auto-park at M0. Reconciliation is R8/group 8 (this is the standing MEDIUM 'projection refusal has no park' carry-forward).
